curation.lead:
Andrew Luxton Horn, known professionally as Drew Horn, is a former U.S. Army Special Forces officer, Deloitte management consultant, and Trump administration national security official who founded GreenMet (Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.) in 2021 to commercialize the critical minerals policy framework he helped create while in government [Finding #6176] [Finding #6200]. At the Department of Energy's Office of International Affairs, Horn served as Chief of Staff and Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary from December 2018 to November 2020, where he led the development of the U.S. critical minerals supply chain strategy. He also served as Country Director for Afghanistan at the Office of the Secretary of Defense, Policy Director for Vice President Pence, and Senior Advisor to the Director of National Intelligence [Finding #6370].

GreenMet's beneficial owners include George Sorial (former Trump Organization EVP and chief compliance counsel) and Keith Schiller (Trump's longtime personal bodyguard and former Director of Oval Office Operations), both of whom resigned board and advisory roles in early 2025 but retain passive minority stakes [Finding #6177] [Finding #6331]. In December 2024, Sorial and Schiller co-founded Javelin Advisors LLC, a government relations firm that registered under FARA to represent Pakistan on a rare earth mineral diplomacy framework valued at an estimated $1 trillion [Finding #6210]. GreenMet's former chief geologist, Ned Mamula, was confirmed as Director of the U.S. Geological Survey in October 2024, the federal agency responsible for designating critical minerals -- a direct revolving-door connection to GreenMet's commercial interests [Finding #6187].

Horn's Greenland operations span rare earth mining and AI infrastructure. GreenMet brokered a strategic partnership with Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S in April 2025, subsequently acquired by Critical Metals Corp (CRML), with a $120 million EXIM Bank letter of intent [Finding #6189]. Through a partnership with Svend Hardenberg's Inuit Development Company, Horn also pursued a 1.5-gigawatt AI data center at Kangerlussuaq -- though the Greenland government told CNBC it had not engaged in dialogue with Horn or GreenMet about the project [Finding #6172]. In January 2025, Horn appeared on Fox and Friends advocating Trump's Greenland acquisition rhetoric while holding active commercial interests on the island [Finding #6180]. Danish intelligence (PET) monitored at least three Trump-connected Americans operating in Greenland for potential covert influence operations; Horn's extensive travel and business activities place him within the same operational ecosystem, though he has not been publicly identified as one of the three [Finding #6190].
curation.system_role: Horn exemplifies the policy-to-profit pathway in which a government official designs a national strategy -- in this case, the U.S. critical minerals supply chain policy -- then leaves government and founds a private company positioned to capture the commercial opportunities that strategy created. His network bridges three contested mineral zones (Greenland, Pakistan, Ukraine) through interlinked entities staffed by Trump inner-circle alumni, with a former colleague now heading the federal agency that designates which minerals receive strategic priority.

sections.title: Military and Government Career
sections.content:
Horn served approximately ten years in the U.S. military, first as a Marine Corps officer with one Iraq deployment (circa 2009), then as an Army Special Forces officer and Green Beret commanding direct-action commando teams across three Afghanistan deployments (circa 2013-2015) [Finding #6176]. He holds a B.A. in Political Science and History from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and an MBA from the University of Virginia's Darden School of Business [Finding #6370].

After transitioning to the private sector as a strategic management consultant at Deloitte Consulting LLP, Horn entered the Trump administration in July 2017 at a starting salary of $112,021 [Finding #6179]. His government career traced a path from combat-zone policy to mineral resource strategy: he served as Country Director for Afghanistan at the Office of the Secretary of Defense (July 2017 to December 2018), where he was instrumental in designing Trump's South Asia Strategy [Finding #6200]. He subsequently served as Policy Director for Vice President Pence, Chief of Staff and Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary at the DOE Office of International Affairs (December 2018 to November 2020), and Senior Advisor to the Director of National Intelligence during the Ratcliffe/Grenell era [Finding #6370]. His financial disclosure upon entering government listed a rental property valued at $100,001 to $250,000 and a Morgan Stanley brokerage account valued at $250,001 to $500,000 [Finding #6179].

The DOE Office of International Affairs role is structurally significant: Horn led the development of the U.S. critical minerals supply chain strategy and intelligence community leadership restructuring [Finding #6200]. He then founded GreenMet in January 2021 -- immediately after leaving government -- to pursue commercial opportunities in precisely the policy domain he had shaped. His Afghanistan portfolio at OSD also connects to the South Asia mineral corridor, the same region where Javelin Advisors now pursues Pakistan's rare earth resources [Finding #6200].

sections.title: GreenMet Corporate Structure and Ownership
sections.content:
GreenMet (formally Greentech Minerals Holdings Inc.) is incorporated in Washington, D.C., with offices at 1825 K Street NW, Suite 515 [Finding #6331]. Horn serves as founder, president, and CEO. The company's other beneficial owners are George Sorial, who spent 17 years as Trump Organization EVP and chief compliance counsel before departing in 2019, and Keith Schiller, Trump's longtime personal bodyguard who served as Director of Oval Office Operations in the first term [Finding #6177]. Both resigned board and advisory roles in early 2025 but remain passive minority shareholders, according to a statement Sorial provided to OCCRP [Finding #6331].

GreenMet's former chief geologist, Ned Mamula -- a former CIA analyst -- was confirmed as Director of the U.S. Geological Survey in October 2024 [Finding #6193]. He filed a divestiture from GreenMet in January 2025 upon Senate confirmation. Horn co-authored the foreword to Mamula's 2024 book Undermining Power [Finding #6187]. The USGS directorship carries authority over critical mineral resource assessments and the Critical Minerals List, which directly affects which projects receive federal support -- a revolving-door connection that runs from GreenMet's scientific staff to the regulatory body overseeing the sector.

George Logothetis's Libra Group invested in GreenMet in March 2022, providing external capital from a Greek-American shipping and infrastructure conglomerate [Connection #3180]. GreenMet has filed 66 LDA lobbying disclosures through 11 registered lobbyists, including via The McKeon Group, which links GreenMet to USA Rare Earth [Finding #6210]. Despite this lobbying activity, no federal contracts have been identified [Finding #6210].

sections.title: Greenland Operations: Rare Earths and Data Center
sections.content:
GreenMet's Greenland footprint emerged in early 2021, with the company's first SSL certificate for greentechminerals.com issued in February of that year [Finding #6189]. The principal Greenland partnership is with Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S, formalized in April 2025, through which GreenMet positioned itself as the intermediary between Greenland rare earth deposits and U.S. defense supply chains [Finding #6197]. Horn visited the Tanbreez mine in May 2025 and met with Greenlandic and Danish officials. By June 2025, Critical Metals Corp (CRML) had secured a $120 million EXIM Bank letter of intent for the Tanbreez project via GreenMet, and by September 2025, CRML took a controlling interest in Tanbreez [Finding #6189]. GreenMet also facilitated a 10-year offtake agreement connecting Tanbreez to a DoD-funded Ucore rare earth processing facility in Louisiana [Finding #6122]. Notably, GreenMet is absent from all 167 CRML SEC filings despite having brokered the deal [Finding #6210].

Separately, Horn pursued a 1.5-gigawatt AI data center at Kangerlussuaq through a partnership between AmForge Corporation and Svend Hardenberg's Inuit Development Company, with a letter of intent signed in January 2026 [Finding #6167]. The project targets 300 megawatts by mid-2027 and 1.5 gigawatts by end of 2028, with GreenMet claiming binding investor commitments for half of each phase [Finding #6172]. However, the Greenland government told CNBC it had not engaged in dialogue with Horn or GreenMet about the project, and no land or local approvals have been secured [Finding #6172].

Hardenberg is a structurally important intermediary. A former Permanent Secretary at the Greenland Premier's Office and former CEO of Greenland's national energy company Nukissiorfiit, he simultaneously sits across multiple competing interests: co-owner of Greenland Water Bank (partly sold to Ronald Lauder's investor consortium), business partner of Horn on the data center and seaweed ventures, and General Manager of Energy Transition Minerals' Greenland subsidiary controlling the separate Kvanefjeld rare earth deposit [Finding #6356] [Finding #6194]. Through Hardenberg, Horn's GreenMet network is one hop from Lauder's Greenland Development Partners LLC consortium [Finding #6204].

sections.title: Javelin Advisors and the Pakistan Mineral Corridor
sections.content:
In December 2024, Horn's GreenMet co-shareholders Sorial and Schiller co-founded Javelin Advisors LLC, a government relations firm that registered under FARA to represent the Government of Pakistan on a rare earth mineral diplomacy framework estimated at $1 trillion [Finding #6210]. Javelin's activities extend beyond Pakistan: the firm has also been involved in Ukraine reconstruction lobbying and NioCorp critical minerals lobbying [Finding #6352]. Separately, Javelin received $200,000 from Logical Strategies LLC -- a firm linked to Giorgi Rtskhiladze -- for asbestos deregulation lobbying [Finding #6352].

The connection between Horn's Afghanistan policy work at OSD and the Javelin Pakistan play is not coincidental. Horn designed the Trump administration's South Asia Strategy while serving as Country Director for Afghanistan [Finding #6200]. Pakistan's rare earth deposits sit within the same South Asia mineral corridor that Horn's policy work addressed. Although Horn is not a named principal of Javelin Advisors, the firm's co-founders are his GreenMet co-shareholders, and the commercial domain -- critical minerals in regions where Horn held policy authority -- is identical [Finding #6210].

sections.title: Public Advocacy, Danish Intelligence, and Conflict of Interest
sections.content:
On January 14, 2025, Horn appeared on Fox and Friends to support Trump's Greenland acquisition rhetoric, stating that Greenlanders are "tired of being exploited and oppressed by the Danes" [Finding #6180]. This media appearance occurred while GreenMet held active business interests in Greenland through the Tanbreez partnership and data center plans, raising questions about whether his public advocacy served his commercial interests.

In November 2023, Horn testified before the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee at a hearing on critical minerals supply chains, warning that "if we don't take corrective action, the situation is dire" regarding U.S. reliance on adversarial nations for critical minerals [Finding #6178]. He advocated federal investment in mineral extraction, refining, and processing -- the same activities GreenMet pursues commercially. Horn also serves as a Senior Fellow at Securing America's Future Energy (SAFE) since September 2021, providing an institutional platform for his policy advocacy [Finding #6176].

In August 2025, Danmarks Radio reported that PET (Danish intelligence) monitored at least three Trump-connected American men for covert influence operations in Greenland, including activities such as compiling lists of pro- and anti-Trump Greenlanders and gathering material to cast Denmark in a negative light in U.S. media [Finding #6190]. While Horn has not been publicly identified as one of the three, his extensive Greenland travel, mining deals, data center negotiations, and media appearances supporting Trump's Greenland rhetoric place him within the same operational ecosystem during the same timeframe. Denmark summoned the U.S. charge d'affaires, and the Danish Defence Intelligence Service's 2025 threat assessment listed the United States as a security concern for the first time, alongside Russia and China [Finding #6190].

sections.title: Financial Profile and Political Donations
sections.content:
Horn's pre-government financial disclosure revealed modest personal wealth: a rental property valued at $100,001 to $250,000 generating $5,001 to $15,000 annually, and a Morgan Stanley brokerage account valued at $250,001 to $500,000 with similar income [Finding #6179]. His starting government salary at the Defense Department was $112,021 [Finding #6179].

FEC donor records contain no matches for Drew Horn, Andrew Horn, or Andrew Luxton Horn in Northern Virginia, nor any donor associated with Deloitte, DOE, or GreenMet [Finding #6184]. The absence of any political donation history is notable for someone who held senior political appointments across four agencies and co-founded a company with two members of Trump's inner circle. This may indicate that Horn's political access derived from professional relationships within the national security establishment rather than donor networks.

Does Horn have any formal or informal advisory role with Javelin Advisors LLC, and was he involved in designing the Pakistan rare earth diplomacy framework that Javelin registered under FARA to pursue?

What is the current status of the Kangerlussuaq data center project, and have any land or environmental approvals been secured from the Greenland government despite its denial of engagement with GreenMet?
